basis: Combined immunodeficiency with characteristic persistent or intermittent neutropenia in most reported patients; recurrent infections alone do not establish respiratory or urinary damage.
Lipid biosynthesis disorder causing progressive neurodegeneration; optic atrophy and impaired vision occur in 30-79%.
Lectin-complement immunodeficiency; necrotizing enterocolitis reported in 2/2 is a separately diagnosed complication rather than established intrinsic bowel involvement.
Glutathione metabolism defect; developmental delay and intellectual disability in 2/2 support CNS involvement. Asthma and eczema are separate diseases; glutathionuria is not renal damage.
Congenital absence of both lower limbs defines a structural musculoskeletal disorder.
Inherited absorptive calcium-handling disorder defined by excessive urinary calcium; no additional organ damage established.
Defining dermal elastic-fiber disease; aortic aneurysm/valvular regurgitation and spinal abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Emphysema and bladder abnormalities are under 30%.
GPI-anchor biosynthesis disorder with profound developmental impairment, seizures and brain abnormalities; joint hypermobility alone does not establish musculoskeletal damage.
Intestinal hypoperistalsis/microcolon and dysfunctional enlarged bladder define the syndrome; urinary tract and kidney abnormalities share the renal axis.
Craniosynostosis and dental defects define disease; papilledema 7/7 and Chiari/syringomyelia 1/2 support eye/CNS involvement. Hearing loss 1/2 and nail dysplasia 1/3 omitted at cap.
Retinal response-recovery disorder causing bradyopsia and reduced visual acuity in all reported patients; no separate neurologic involvement established.
Lysosomal storage neurodegeneration with dementia, seizures and motor decline; retinal degeneration is variable and not established as common across adult subtypes.
Lysosomal disease with neurodegeneration and ichthyosis; visual impairment 80-99% with optic/retinal lesions. Skeletal and hearing damage 30-79% omitted at cap; organomegaly alone insufficient.
Purine overproduction; renal insufficiency reported in 30-79%. Neurologic/hearing findings are enriched in the severe subtype; mild disease predominates. Gout and stones are separate diagnoses.
Psychiatric sexual-response disorder without a defining disease of any covered organ axis.
Renal failure, sensorineural deafness and parathyroid hyperplasia define the syndrome; bone cysts occur in 30-79%. Anemia is under 30%.
DTNA-associated ventricular myocardial noncompaction, often with congenital cardiac defects; all established manifestations remain cardiovascular.
Structural deficiency of dental enamel; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
FMO3-related trimethylamine metabolism defect; odor does not imply skin damage or hepatic dysfunction, and associated emotional symptoms do not establish neurologic injury.
Inherited palmoplantar hyperkeratosis with blistering and ulceration; chronic tinea is a separate infection rather than an intrinsic immune disorder.
Defined autoimmune injury of the musculoskeletal system; subtype-specific cardiac or skin disease does not apply across the umbrella.
Recurrent encephalopathy with ataxia, spasticity and abnormal reflexes; muscle stiffness is neurologic, and joint hypermobility alone does not establish locomotor damage.
Neurometabolic disorder with lactic acidosis and CNS dysfunction; supplied HPO reports osteolytic toe defects in 30-79%. Hypotonia and tachypnea alone do not establish muscle or lung injury.
Adult cutaneous non-Langerhans histiocytic proliferation; systemic, ocular and marrow involvement are not common defining features.
Ichthyosis, hepatomegaly and cerebellar degeneration define the syndrome; splenic enlargement is also a defining feature, reported in 80-99%. Metabolic mechanism is unestablished.
